text:
morgan: Heads up — onboarding sampleapp CI started failing regen diffs on master after the auth/retry tweak. It’s a tiny ordering/optional-param noise but blocks publishing the samplekit.

sam: Repro steps? I can take a look.

morgan: Checkout master, run: `yarn regen && git status --porcelain`. Diff shows `TypeGen: reorder optional params` even though codegen output should be stable. Also noticed auth header retry wrapper got folded into the client constructor in TS SDK which changes import ordering. Example snippet from regen:```diff
- export type FooParams = { a: string; b?: number }
+ export type FooParams = { b?: number; a: string }
```

rita: ugh. I saw nondet sorts before when we pulled in a new prettier/ts-generator. Could be sort order in `typegen` when constructing properties + JS object enumeration.

ci-bot: CI: regen-check failed on job #4821 — https://ci.redwood.ai/4821/logs (exit code 1) :warning:

alex: I reproduced locally — looks like two things: 1) our auth retry change added a tiny helper that inserts optional params via Object.assign which doesn't guarantee property order, and 2) the typegen key sorting only runs for top-level props, not nested mapped types. Combined they flip output.

morgan: Good call. For a quick unblock I pushed a shim to sampleapp that pins a deterministic sort in the typegen step: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/231 (WIP). That gets CI green but it feels fragile.

sam: Long term we should: 1) make typegen emit sorted keys deterministicly (explicit sort in codegen), 2) avoid relying on Object.assign for param assembly in the auth wrapper, and 3) add a regen unit test in samplekit.

rita: Agreed. Also need to check semver implications — the auth wrapper change went in as a patch but it touched surface area of SDK constructors. If we change typegen layout again we might force a minor.

jamie: Quick checklist I propose: - create a small failing test reproducing ordering nondeterminism (in typegen tests) - add deterministic sort in the generator - revert the Object.assign usage in auth-retry PR and replace with explicit key assembly - run regen across all sampleapps before publishing. I'll own tests + regen run.

morgan: @jamie thanks — can you open the test PR and link here? I'll hold the sampleapp publish until we have a stable regen.

jamie: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/typegen/pull/88 — includes deterministic sort and a unit that repros the previous flip. Ran locally with `yarn test` and `yarn regen` — stable now.

sam: Nice. I'll update the auth/retry PR to avoid Object.assign and keep the shim until typegen patch ships.

ci-bot: CI: rerun triggered for sampleapp job #4821.

morgan: CI green for sampleapp + typegen tests. Thanks team :tada:

rita: Follow-up: let's add a regen-check to the SDK publish job so we catch these earlier — filing ticket.

morgan: filing: https://tracker.redwood.ai/ISSUE-712 — regen-check in publish pipeline.

sam: moving to close when PRs merge.

alex: FYI leaving a short note in the changelog draft about the auth wrapper internal change (no public API break expected).

morgan: cool. closing thread when sampleapp publish goes through.
